utilities.name: Sulphur Springs Valley E C Inc

why: The site is within Tucson city limits, so the Pima County moratorium on unincorporated areas does not apply. However, the 300 MW facility's assumed 121 diesel generators (2500 kW each) yield an estimated NOx potential to emit of 1,067 tpy, exceeding the 100 tpy major-source threshold and triggering a federal Title V operating permit requirement. This major air permit requirement is costly and slow but does not block the project outright, so the project can proceed conditionally upon securing the Title V permit.

findings.reason: applies only to unincorporated areas; site is inside a city

evidence.quote: Board of Supervisors adopted a 120-day moratorium on new data center permit applications in unincorporated Pima County while the county finalizes a data-center zoning code amendment.

Active as of 2026-09-23. 120-day moratorium on the acceptance/issuance of new data center permits in unincorporated Pima County, adopted 3-2 (Supervisors Christy and Scott dissenting) on 2026-08-11 and running to approximately 2026-12-09, while Development Services finalizes a zoning code text amendment. The department is seeking public comment (online survey; a September 28, 2026 open house; proposed rules going to the Planning and Zoning Commission on October 28, 2026) on a related, permanent zoning code amendment that would define data centers (facilities using more than 20 MW), require closed-loop cooling, and set review/design standards; that permanent amendment is expected in December 2026, around when the moratorium runs out.

state_watch.key_provisions: Section 31 imposes a three-year moratorium, 2026-07-01 through 2029-06-30, on new applications to the state data center tax relief program under A.R.S. 41-1519. It suspends eligibility for the incentive; it does not pause data center construction, siting, or local permitting.
